summary: Round 9 verifies the two round-8 fixes by mutation in my own tree rather than accepting them, and both hold. (1) The new test theBOUNDEDCrossingSTOPSAtTheBarrierReachedThroughAnUncheckpointedEpoch genuinely routes through the SECOND crossFromCheckpoint call site, not the first: widening the walk's own probe (`crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit)` after a CONTINUE) to Long.MAX_VALUE now fails EXACTLY that one test, and widening the FIRST hop's `crossFromCheckpoint(hops, epoch, upTo)` fails aCheckpointCoveringEntriesPASTTheBarrierIsNotUsed and theBOUNDEDCrossingStillStopsAtTheSlotTheCONTINUENamed while leaving the new test green. The two tests net disjoint sites, which is what the round-8 blocker asked for. (2) The `chainEpoch == ownEpoch` guard is now killed: `if (true)` fails the new nextSequence assertion with 41 against 1 -- measured, and the failure message confirms it is that assertion and not one of its neighbours. (3) The THIRD call site is genuinely nothing to pin: `limit = Long.MAX_VALUE` is assigned unconditionally two lines above it in the neverOpened branch, so the barrier-widening mutant there is textually the same value -- an equivalent mutant, not an untested one. That branch's MAX_VALUE barrier is also pre-existing (the assignment is unchanged context in this diff), so this commit does not enlarge the suffix it admits; it only lets a checkpoint terminate the same walk. Also verified: the `chainEpoch == ownEpoch` guard can only be TRUE at site 1, since chainEpoch strictly decreases from ownEpoch at sites 2 and 3 and `inherited()` sets ownEpoch to Long.MIN_VALUE -- so the new assertion pins the only reachable-true instance. (4) Nothing broke: full `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL in my own copy of the staged bytes, and the suite counts 788 tests, matching the row's claim exactly. (5) The row's new rule -- state the property, never the census -- is itself durable prose and cannot go stale; ADR-0035 now states the property rather than enumerating tests. But the same delta reintroduces the census form one file over, which is the minor below. No production source changed since the round-8 verdict, so the request-rate lens is unchanged: the walk still costs one stat per epoch probed and terminates at the first ancestor holding a usable checkpoint, scaling with epochs walked and never with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.title: The new assertion's `.as()` label names the wrong chain, and gives a reason that is not the reason
findings.failure_scenario: The assertion is `reader.nextSequence()` where `reader` is `new CommitLog(counting, PREFIX, 4)` -- the chain being recovered is epoch 4, whose slot 0 holds the CONTINUE written by `epoch4.open(3, burnedAt)`, which is why the next slot is 1. The label says `epoch 3 is empty, so its next slot is its own, not epoch 1's`. Epoch 3 IS empty, but that is not what makes this 1: epoch 4's own slot 0 does, and the answer would still be 1 if epoch 3 were full. A maintainer who later changes the fixture's burned run (this test is named for a RUN of burned epochs and the row records that it was once wrong by burning only one) reads the label, believes the assertion is about the burned chain, and adjusts the expected value against epoch 3 rather than epoch 4 -- weakening or deleting the only assertion in the tree that kills `if (true)` on the `chainEpoch == ownEpoch` seeding guard. This is the same shape as the `.as()` label M4.8c's rounds caught claiming coverage that did not exist. Measured: under the mutant the failure prints `[epoch 3 is empty, so its next slot is its own, not epoch 1's] expected: 1L but was: 41L`, so the label is what a future failure is diagnosed from.
findings.suggestion: Name epoch 4 and its CONTINUE: `epoch 4 holds only its own CONTINUE, so its next slot is 1 -- not epoch 1's 41`. Recording it in the commit body is the right response under review.md `minors-land`; a tenth round spent on a comment is the pathology this task has already paid for.

findings.title: The fix for the stale census restates a census: `THREE CALL SITES ... this test nets the FIRST; its sibling below nets the second`
findings.failure_scenario: The backlog row this delta rewrites concludes that the rule which finally held is to state the PROPERTY and never the census, because a sentence counting things elsewhere is falsified by the next commit that moves one. The comment rewritten in the same delta does exactly that in a new dimension: it counts call sites in ChainReplay (`THREE`) and inventories which test nets which (`this test nets the FIRST; its sibling below nets the second`). That sentence has already been falsified once -- it said TWICE, and the row records that the undercount is why the second site had no net. M5's forwarding or M4.23's origin work adds a fourth construction of the barrier; the comment still reads THREE, and a reader auditing whether every site is netted is told by a confident, wrong census that they are. The census is also unenforced -- no gate counts `crossFromCheckpoint` call sites -- so it goes stale silently, which is the exact property the row says makes the form unusable. The durable form states the property instead: every construction of the barrier needs its own net, and here is where each of the two existing ones lives.
findings.suggestion: Record, do not fix. Under review.md `minors-land` this lands in the commit body; the sentence has now been redrafted twice and the row itself observes that patching such a sentence produces a fresh one with the same property. If it is ever rewritten, the property form -- `every site that constructs this barrier needs its own test; a site with no test is a silent I3` -- is what survives a fourth site appearing.
